### Position read
The opponent opened by advancing an edge piece to (3,3). We answered with our right-edge piece to (3,4), splitting the upper center. No losses or eliminations have occurred.

### Our plan
Keep at least one center square secured while bringing our left-edge color toward (4,3) or (4,4). Look for same-color sandwich setups; never assume our two colors can flank together. Avoid friendly-fire lines through our own teammate.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent immediately prioritized direct center occupation, suggesting a fast center race.

### Lessons
A center foothold prevents an instant four-square occupation and forces the opponent to dislodge us. Recalculate captures only from each landing square.

### Position read
We hold (3,4); the opponent holds (3,3) and (4,3). Our new piece at (2,5) blocks the direct descent from (0,5) to (3,5), preventing an immediate same-color sandwich of our center piece. No losses or eliminations yet.

### Our plan
Preserve (3,4) and contest the last center square. Consider placing one of our center-holder color at (5,3), then later moving another to (2,3): if the opponent leaves pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), that same-color sandwich captures both. Keep (5,3) and its approach lane clear.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is racing both colors directly into adjacent central squares and may seek a same-color flank around our blocker.

### Lessons
Before every move, scan for one-move sandwiches against occupied center squares. A blocker anywhere on a rook path can prevent the capturing landing square from being reached.

### Position read
We hold (3,4); the opponent holds (3,3) and (4,3). Red at (3,6) threatens to move to (3,5), sandwiching our center piece against Red at (3,3). Our Blue move to (4,5) blocks Yellow's direct route from (7,5) toward (3,5). No losses or eliminations yet.

### Our plan
On Green's turn, if legal, move Green (2,5) to (3,5), physically blocking Red's capturing landing square. Then preserve the Blue center holder and seek a same-color flank against Red at (3,6). Blue can later establish at (3,7), and after Green vacates (3,5), a Blue move from (3,4) to (3,5) would capture Red at (3,6).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating both colors in and around the center and has begun creating same-color sandwich geometry rather than merely occupying squares.

### Lessons
Defend threatened pieces by controlling the attacker's landing square. Account for intervening opponent turns: blocking Yellow's access to (3,5) makes the intended Green defense more reliable.

### Position read
We hold (3,4) with Blue and now (3,5) with Green. The opponent holds (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4), so the center remains contested. Green at (3,5) blocks Red at (3,6) from landing there and sandwiching our Blue piece against Red at (3,3). No losses or eliminations yet.

### Our plan
Preserve our two adjacent pieces on row 3 and prevent the opponent from completing the center. Seek Blue same-color flanking geometry against Red at (3,6), potentially by establishing Blue at (3,7). If Green later vacates (3,5), Blue may move from (3,4) to (3,5) to capture Red at (3,6), provided a Blue far flank exists.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating both colors in the center and using Red pieces on row 3 to threaten sandwiches. Yellow has advanced directly into (4,4), increasing the urgency of center denial.

### Lessons
An occupied attack square can stop an otherwise immediate sandwich. Always check whether moving that blocker later exposes the protected piece, and watch for instant center victory after every move.

### Position read
Blue moved (5,7) to (5,4), sandwiching and capturing Yellow at (4,4) against Blue at (3,4). Yellow now has 1 loss; all other loss counts are 0. After the capture, the center has opponent pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), our Blue at (3,4), and (4,4) empty. Green remains at (3,5), protecting the row-3 structure.

### Our plan
Keep denying center occupation while exploiting same-color flanks. Blue at (3,4) and (5,4) create vertical capture potential if an opponent enters (4,4): a future Blue move cannot capture merely because the sandwich exists, so we must trigger it by landing elsewhere appropriately or re-forming the line. Green should maintain pressure beside the center and avoid exposing Blue at (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has concentrated both colors around the four central squares. Expect Yellow to refill (4,4) or reposition from (4,3), and Red to seek a way around Green’s blocker at (3,5).

### Lessons
Look for captures formed by an existing friendly far flank: landing at (5,4) used Blue at (3,4) to remove the intervening center piece. Captures require our triggering move; static sandwiches do nothing.

### Position read
Our Green moved (3,5) to (2,5), defusing the immediate opponent move (2,6)->(3,6), which would have sandwiched and captured our pieces at (3,5) and (3,4) against the opponent at (3,3). Center remains: opponent at (3,3),(4,3), ours at (3,4), and (4,4) empty. Losses: opponent Yellow 1, all others 0.

### Our plan
If the opponent plays (0,4)->(2,4), capturing our Green at (2,5) against its (2,6), answer on Blue’s turn with (1,7)->(1,4): the landing sandwiches the new opponent piece at (2,4) against our Blue at (3,4). Continue denying all-opponent center occupation while building same-color flanks.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating around the center and may prioritize tactical sandwiches involving the piece at (3,3). Watch moves landing on row 3 to exploit that far flank.

### Lessons
Mixed-color lines are capturable when bounded by one moving color. Evacuating the adjacent piece can break a dangerous line; choose the evacuation square to create a recapture if pursued.

### Position read
We moved Blue (4,5)->(4,4). The center is fully occupied but split: opponent at (3,3),(4,3), ours at (3,4),(4,4), so neither team wins. Vacating (4,5) prevents the opponent’s Yellow (7,6)->(4,6) from sandwiching our center pair. Losses: opponent Yellow 1; all others 0.

### Our plan
Protect our Blue at (3,4) from opponent Red (3,6)->(3,5), which would capture it against Red (3,3). On Green’s turn, if (3,5) is empty, strongly consider Green (2,5)->(3,5) to block that landing; moving into the bracket is safe. If the opponent occupies (3,5), it already blocks the Red capture. Hold both right center squares and seek same-color flanks against the opponent’s two left-center pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent concentrates pieces around the center and builds same-color sandwich endpoints. Check every accessible landing beside our central pieces, especially rows 3 and 4.

### Lessons
Before filling a gap between pieces, inspect whether it completes an opponent sandwich line. Moving the former endpoint into the gap can gain occupation while breaking the dangerous line.

### Position read
We moved Green (2,5)->(3,5), blocking Red (3,6)->(3,5), which would have captured our Blue at (3,4) against Red (3,3). Center: opponent holds (3,3),(4,3); we hold (3,4); (4,4) is empty. Losses: our Blue 1, opponent Yellow 1, others 0.

### Our plan
If still safe on Blue’s turn, consider Blue (5,4)->(4,4) to restore both right-center squares. Green endpoints now sit at (3,0) and (3,5); landing a Green at (3,2) would sandwich Yellow (3,1) leftward and the mixed Red (3,3)+Blue (3,4) rightward, trading one Blue loss for losses to both opponent colors. First determine whether that friendly-fire trade is worthwhile and whether the opponent disrupts the row.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is actively using same-color endpoints near the center; Yellow used (4,3) to capture our Blue at (4,4). Expect attempts to reopen (3,5) or build another bracket around our center pieces.

### Lessons
A blocking piece may both prevent an immediate sandwich and become a far endpoint for a later multi-direction capture. Recheck all four rays after every central move, including friendly-fire costs.

### Position read
We moved Blue (5,4)->(4,4). Center now has opponent pieces at (3,3),(4,3) and ours at (3,4),(4,4). Losses: our Blue 1; opponent Yellow 1; others 0. Red retreated from (3,6) to (2,6), leaving Green (3,5) in place.

### Our plan
Preserve the two right-center squares and watch for Yellow attempts to dislodge Blue (4,4). On Green’s turn, seek moves that constrain the opponent’s two left-center pieces without exposing our Blue pieces to same-color brackets. Build reachable Green endpoints before attempting a row-3 sandwich.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is actively contesting the center and previously used Yellow endpoints to capture Blue at (4,4). Red withdrew when its direct row-3 capture route was blocked.

### Lessons
The earlier proposed Green landing at (3,2) is currently impossible: pieces at (3,4) and (3,3) block Green from (3,5), while Yellow at (3,1) blocks Green from (3,0). Always verify the entire travel path before planning a sandwich.

### Position read
We moved (3,5)->(1,5). The center remains split: the opponent occupies (3,3),(4,3), while we occupy (3,4),(4,4). Our piece at (1,5) blocks the opponent’s top-edge piece from landing at (3,5), so the upper-center piece cannot be immediately sandwiched. Losses remain ours 1, opponent 1.

### Our plan
Expect the opponent to capture our piece at (4,4) by landing at (4,5); preserve the piece at (3,4) and then contest the vacated lower-center square. Use the advanced piece at (1,5) to constrain the top edge or descend again when the central file clears.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent coordinates same-color endpoints carefully and attacks occupied center squares immediately when a landing square opens. They withdrew a direct upper capture threat only to retain another route.

### Lessons
Moving to (4,5) would fail: the opponent could first capture (3,4), then land at (4,6) and sandwich both (4,5) and (4,4). When defending one center square, check whether the blocker completes a longer opposing sandwich.

### Position read
We moved our lower-center piece from (4,4) to (4,5). Our piece at (3,4) remains exposed: the opponent can land at (3,5) from (2,5) and sandwich it against (3,3). Losses are currently ours 2 total across our colors and the opponent 1.

### Our plan
Our piece at (4,5) blocks the immediate lower sandwich and threatens the opponent piece at (5,5): moving our piece from (6,7) to (6,5) would capture it against (4,5). Use the next move of our other color to improve central access, though it cannot presently stop the upper-center capture. Preserve the surviving normal piece because one more loss would eliminate that color.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent rapidly removes blockers to reopen coordinated same-color sandwich routes. Expect them to move the threatened piece at (5,5), or accept its loss while preparing a counter-sandwich around (4,5).

### Lessons
When two center pieces are both under sequential capture, save the one whose escape square also creates tempo. A defensive landing can be stronger when it denies the attack square and establishes a sandwich threat.

### Position read
We moved the acting piece from (1,0) to (1,4), opening a direct route down column 4. The opponent can now move (2,5) to (3,5), sandwiching our piece at (3,4) against (3,3); that would raise that color's losses to 2. The opponent's latest piece at (6,6) blocks our former capture route from (6,7) to (6,5).

### Our plan
After the expected upper-center capture, preserve the vulnerable color's remaining pieces and avoid placing one at (4,4), where the opponent can answer from (5,5) to (4,5) and sandwich it against (4,3). On our next acting-color turn, use (1,4) to occupy the newly cleared (3,4), contesting the center safely. Look for ways to dislodge the opponent's pieces at (3,3) and (4,3).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent anticipates sandwich threats and blocks landing lanes before they become captures. Expect the immediate upper-center sandwich and continued use of the two center-left pieces as stationary flanks.

### Lessons
Recheck every proposed rook route for newly inserted blockers. When one color approaches its third loss, center occupation must be screened for an immediate same-color counter-sandwich.

### Position read
Blue has 2 losses and must avoid any further capture. We moved Blue from (2,7) to (3,7), keeping it away from the Red flanks on columns 4-5 while gaining lateral access along row 3. Current key pieces: ours at (1,4), (3,0), (4,0), (5,0), (6,0), Blue at (1,7), (3,7), (4,5), (6,7); opponent center pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), with Red also at (3,5).

### Our plan
On the coming Green turn, play (1,4) to (3,4) if the route and destination remain clear. This contests the center and is not immediately sandwiched by the stationary Reds at (3,3)/(3,5), because captures trigger only from the mover’s landing square. Keep Blue away from (4,4): Yellow can answer by landing at (4,5) from (5,5) once that square is vacated or available, using (4,3) as the far flank.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent promptly takes available sandwiches and blocks developing capture lanes. Expect a Yellow move aimed at obstructing or preparing against Green’s entry to (3,4).

### Lessons
With Blue one loss from elimination, screen every destination against both the next Yellow move and the following Red move. Preserve the Green column-4 route and remember that merely entering an existing sandwich is safe.

### Position read

On Blue’s next turn, urgently evacuate (4,5), normally to (4,6) or (4,7): otherwise Yellow can play (6,6)->(4,6), sandwiching it against Yellow (4,4) and eliminating Blue. Preserve Green (3,4) as a center blocker and seek occupation of (4,3) only after neutralizing Yellow’s (7,2)->(4,2) capture resource.

The opponent actively prepares sandwiches and has just moved Yellow to (4,4), creating the direct threat against Blue (4,5). Expect Red to constrain Blue’s escape or improve central control.

Existing enemy flanks do not capture a piece that moves between them. With Blue one loss from elimination, prioritize immediate capture threats over development.

### Position read
Blue at (4,5) escaped to (4,6), directly blocking Yellow’s planned (6,6)->(4,6) sandwich. Blue remains at 2 losses, with pieces at (1,7), (3,7), (4,6), and (6,7). The center is now ours at (3,4), opponent at (4,3) and (4,4), with (3,3) empty.

Keep Blue alive above all; watch for new one-move sandwiches against (4,6). Preserve Green (3,4) as the central blocker. Seek (3,3) or eventual (4,3) occupation only when capture-safe, while using Blue’s right-edge formation to restrict opponent movement.

The opponent prepares direct sandwiches and has increased central control by moving Red from (3,3) to (4,3). Expect Yellow to redirect after its capture threat was blocked.

Occupying an opponent’s intended landing square can neutralize a sandwich cleanly. Blue is still one loss from elimination, so every Blue move requires an immediate capture-threat scan.

The center now has opponent pieces at (4,3) and (4,4), while (3,3) and (3,4) are empty. Our vulnerable color remains at 2 losses with pieces on the right side.

Prioritize eliminating the opponent color now on 2 losses while keeping our own 2-loss color safe. Prevent the opponent from completing the center, especially if (3,4) is occupied next. Seek a safe occupation of (3,3), but scan for same-color far flanks before entering.

### Lessons
The former piece at (3,4) was vulnerable to a same-color sandwich using the opponent pieces at (4,3) and (3,5). Tactical captures that also evacuate threatened pieces are preferable to static center occupation.

### Position read

Keep (3,4) occupied or otherwise break the opponent’s three-square center formation. On our next turn, look for a tactical capture of the opponent’s 2-loss color, especially around (4,4), (5,4), and (6,6). Avoid exposing our 2-loss color to a third capture; use our safer color to reinforce or disrupt central lines.

When the opponent holds three center squares, occupying the fourth is mandatory unless one of their existing center pieces can be removed immediately. Recheck sandwich geometry after every central move because mixed-color lines can all be captured by same-color endpoints.

A teammate-colored blocker can be sandwiched as part of a mixed line. After elimination, Void pieces still count for center but cannot capture, so verify whether any can physically occupy the threatened center square.
